task.text: The app asks one `KeyValue`; the ambassador handles shards, retries and timeouts for it.
Implement `Ambassador implements KeyValue` in `Ambassador.java`. `KeyValue` and `ProfileService` are given and must not change.

items: `Ambassador(List<List<KeyValue>> shards, int attempts, long timeoutMs)`: the shard of a key is `Math.floorMod(key.hashCode(), shards.size())`; replicas are tried in order.
Each replica gets up to `attempts` tries. An `IOException`, or a try that takes longer than `timeoutMs`, counts as a failure; then retry, then try the next replica.
When all are exhausted, throw `IOException` whose message starts `shard N unavailable` and whose cause is the last failure.
A `RuntimeException` from a replica is a bug: it propagates at once, with no retry.

checks.title: A key goes to its shard
A healthy call is made once
A dead shard gives a clear IOException
The ambassador implements the same port
The application knows nothing of it

hints.text: The ambassador is the same interface as the thing it fronts, so the app cannot tell the difference. Two nested loops: replicas outside, tries inside. Which failures deserve a retry?

For the timeout, run each try on its own thread (a virtual thread is cheap) completing a `CompletableFuture`, and `get(timeoutMs, MILLISECONDS)`. Map `TimeoutException` to an `IOException` so the retry logic is one path.

lines: throw new IOException("shard " + shard + " unavailable", last);
